Title: Kotlin tutorial — Lily Design System

Description: Build an accessible contact form in Jetpack Compose with Lily's Kotlin libraries: your words in, Lily's semantics and accessibility out, and a theme that never changes what TalkBack reads.

# Kotlin tutorial

Lily's semantics, accessibility contracts and worldwide rules for Jetpack Compose on Android: every word is yours, every native control stays Material's, and a theme changes how a component looks, never what TalkBack reads.

## What you'll build

A small contact form — a labelled field with a hint and an error, an error summary, a warning — first plain, then themed, in about 15 minutes.

**Early and unreleased.** The Kotlin libraries are not on Maven Central yet, so you build them from a copy of the monorepo. Their components are a first slice, not the whole catalog: see the list in step 2.

## Before you start

You need a JDK 17 or later, an Android SDK with platform 37.2 (Compose 1.13 requires it and `minSdk` 24), Kotlin 2.4 and an app built with Jetpack Compose. The components use `compose.foundation` and `compose.ui` only: Lily never depends on Material.

## Step 1 — Add the libraries

```
git clone https://github.com/LilyDesignSystem/lily-design-system
```

Until there is a release, the supported way to use the libraries is as modules of the repository's own Gradle build, `lily-design-system-kotlin`. Open it in Android Studio, add your app as a module (`include(":my-app")` in its `settings.gradle.kts`) and depend on the Lily modules by project, as the example app does:

```
// my-app/build.gradle.kts
dependencies {
    implementation(project(":lily-compose"))
    implementation(project(":lily-compose-themes"))
    // …your Compose BOM, foundation and activity-compose, as in lily-compose-examples-app
}
```

The modules are `lily-core` (Kotlin Multiplatform, no Android dependency: search folding, middle truncation, clinical formatting), `lily-compose` (the components), `lily-compose-themes` (generated tokens and `LilyTheme`) and `lily-compose-examples` (a worked example of every component). `lily-compose-examples-app` is a complete app to copy from.

## Step 2 — Your first component

```
import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import io.github.lilydesignsystem.compose.WarningText

@Composable
fun Notice() {
    WarningText(prefix = "Warning", text = "You can be fined up to £5,000 if you do not register.")
}
```

`WarningText` keeps the prefix and the text together so TalkBack reads them as one sentence. The first slice has `Field`, `ErrorSummary`, `SummaryList`, `WarningText`, `LilyAlert`, `LilyBadge`, `Tag`, `LilyCard`, `InsetText`, `Disclosure`, the clinical views and the International Patient Summary. Lily ships no button, switch, checkbox, slider, date picker, sheet or navigation: on Compose those are Material 3's.

## Step 3 — Compose a small form

```
import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column
import androidx.compose.foundation.text.BasicTextField
import androidx.compose.runtime.*
import io.github.lilydesignsystem.compose.*

@Composable
fun ContactForm() {
    var name by remember { mutableStateOf("") }
    var nameError by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
    Column {
        nameError?.let { ErrorSummary(title = "There is a problem", problems = listOf(Problem(it) { /* focus the field */ })) }
        Field(label = "Full name", description = "As it appears on your passport", error = nameError,
              required = true, requiredLabel = "required") { fieldModifier ->
            BasicTextField(value = name, onValueChange = { name = it }, modifier = fieldModifier)
        }
        WarningText(prefix = "Warning", text = "You can be fined up to £5,000 if you do not register.")
    }
}
```

`Field` draws the visible label, the hint and the error, and hands its control a `Modifier` that carries the spoken name and the error: apply it to the control. `ErrorSummary` lists the problems and calls each one's lambda when it is activated, so you can move focus to the field.

**Verified 2026-11-22:** this form and the theme in step 5 were compiled against the modules with Gradle (`compileDebugKotlin`). The accessibility checks of the example app run on an emulator (see step 6).

## Step 4 — The Compose idioms

- **Every word is yours.** Lily has no default text and no string resources: labels, hints and errors are parameters, so the form speaks your app's language.
- **Pass the modifier to the control.** `Field` gives its content a `Modifier`; a control that ignores it loses its spoken name.
- **Text follows the user.** Text styles come from `LocalLilyTextStyles`, which defaults to the platform's text, so the user's font scale applies unchanged.
- **Spoken joins are line breaks**, never words or punctuation of Lily's own, and tappable parts are at least 48 by 48 dp.

## Step 5 — Theme it

Add `lily-compose-themes` and wrap the content once:

```
import androidx.compose.foundation.isSystemInDarkTheme
import io.github.lilydesignsystem.compose.themes.LilyTheme
import io.github.lilydesignsystem.compose.themes.LilyTokens

@Composable
fun Root() {
    LilyTheme(if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) LilyTokens.dark else LilyTokens.govUk) { ContactForm() }
}
```

The tokens are `LilyTokens.light`, `dark`, `nhsEnglandPatients`, `govUk`, `uswds` and `japanDigitalAgency`, generated from the same token files as the web themes. A theme decorates through `LocalLilyDecoration`, applied after each component's semantics, so it can change how a component looks but never what TalkBack reads. Text uses only the colour pairs the web themes gate at 4.5:1. Using a public-sector theme does not make your app that body's service: supply your own name and marks.

## Step 6 — See it all working

`lily-compose-examples` has a worked example of every component and a searchable catalog you can host in your own activity; navigation stays yours:

```
setContent {
    var selected by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
    BackHandler(enabled = selected != null) { selected = null }
    ExampleCatalog(title = "Components", searchLabel = "Search components", selected = selected, onSelect = { selected = it })
}
```

Or install the ready-made example app on a device or emulator; its accessibility test runs Google's Accessibility Test Framework over the catalog and every detail view at font scale 1.0 and 2.0:

```
cd lily-design-system/lily-design-system-kotlin
./gradlew :lily-compose-examples-app:installDebug
```
